base_source: Continuing-ops TTM through Q2 2026 from EDGAR 10-Q YTD: consolidated OCF TTM $2,624M (FY25 $3,057M - H1'25 $1,473M + H1'26 $1,040M) minus discontinued-ops OCF TTM $712M (FY25 $1,185M - H1'25 $581M + H1'26 $108M) = continuing OCF $1,912M; minus continuing capex TTM $218M and total SBC TTM $84M = OE $1,610M / 436M H1'26 diluted shares = $3.6927. Engine normalized median base $6.41 rejected: it capitalises the Fiber Business sold 2026-05-01 (its $1,185M FY25 OCF is in consolidated OCF) while the capex tag is continuing-basis and never charges fiber's ~$1B/yr build capex.
method_range_note: Basis break (Fiber/Small Cell sold 2026-05-01 for ~$8.4B net; >$7B debt repaid, $1B buyback) makes every filed base straddle a sold business. Preliminary engine run on the distorted $6.41 mixed-basis base: weighted IRR 8.9%, IV@15% $41.79 (Tier D). Headline continuing TTM base $3.69: 7.5%, $31.30 (D). Interest-adjusted continuing sensitivity ($4.24/sh, adding ~$240M/yr run-rate interest savings): 8.2%, $35.97 (D). All defensible bases are Tier D. Engine net debt ($27.0B) is pre-sale; Q2 2026 post-sale net debt is $17,197M = 10.7x continuing OE / ~6.4x guided EBITDA. Confidence low per SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH (REIT) rule; AFFO cross-check (17.3x guided AFFO, 5.3% dividend yield + ~2-3% growth) independently agrees with Tier D.
moat_justification: Scarce permitted tower sites with real relocation switching costs, ~6-yr weighted-average contract term, $23.7B contracted amounts and ~3% escalators, plus pure-play US scale — against extreme tenant concentration (AT&T ~28% of site rental revenue; Sprint cancellations and DISH terminations still shrinking reported revenue), no pricing power beyond escalators, US carrier capex ex-growth, a ~93% AFFO dividend payout that retains nothing, and a fiber decade that ended in a ~$5B impairment.
name: Crown Castle Inc.
one_liner: Pure-play US tower REIT after the fiber exit, moat 6/10 — contracted escalator rents are real, but at $79.56 you pay 17.3x guided AFFO and 21.6x continuing TTM owner's earnings ($3.69/share) for ~3% underlying growth, a ~93% dividend payout and still ~6.4x leverage; weighted IRR 7.5% (IV@15% $31.30), so it clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$31 — roughly $36 on the most generous interest-adjusted base.
